report: A 5-month-old girl with normal prior development developed fever, then a 10–15-hour refractory seizure and persistent left hemiparesis that improved with antiepileptics. MRI right hemicerebral diffusion restriction with normal left cortex and normal MRA indicates unilateral postictal edema, not large-vessel stroke; normal MRA argues against acute ischemic stroke. The prolonged focal seizure is atypical for infectious meningoencephalitis. These features best fit hemiconvulsion-hemiplegia. EEG, CSF, and follow-up MRI are unavailable, so confidence is 0.8.
